title: Diaper-Change Log and Health Signal
dataSources: Baby feeds (`baby:feed`), baby sleep (`baby:sleep`), diaper changes (`diaper:change`), chore completions (`chore:completion`), allowance ledger (`allowance:ledger`), family calendar (`family:calendar`), growth measurements (`growth:measurement`).
app: Baby-tracking apps (Huckleberry/Baby Daybook exports), chore and allowance boards, shared family calendars, and growth logs — sent to Splunk HEC via scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=diaper:change
| bin _time span=1d
| stats sum(eval(if(type="wet",1,0))) as wet, sum(eval(if(type="dirty",1,0))) as dirty by _time
| eval low_wet=if(wet<6,1,0)
| sort - _time
description: Counts daily wet and dirty nappies, a simple but genuine indicator of a newborn's hydration and feeding.
value: Too few wet nappies is an early dehydration warning parents are told to watch; a running count makes it hard to miss.
implementation: Log diaper changes to `index=personal`; schedule daily and flag days with unusually few wet nappies.
visualization: Column chart of daily wet versus dirty nappies.
grandmaExplanation: It counts the baby's nappies each day, which is a simple way to check they are feeding and hydrated well.
